edition.name: Migne, Patrologia Latina 5 (1844), via Latin Wikisource
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Dat tuba coelo signum, sublato leone; Et fiunt subito tenebrae cum coeli fragore. Summittit oculos Dominus ut terra tremiscat; Adclamat ut et audiant omnes in orbem: Ecce diu tacui sufferens tanto tempore vestra. Conclamant pariter plangentes sero gementes; Ululatur, ploratur, nec spatium datur iniquis. Lactanti quid faciet mater? cum ipsa crematur. In flamma ignis Dominus judicabit iniquos: Justos autem non tanget ignis, sed immo delinget. Sub uno morantur, sed pars in sententia flevit. Tantus erit ardor, ut lapides ipsi liquescant; In fulmina coeunt venti, furit ira coelestis, Ut quacumque fugit impius, occupatur ab igne. Suppetium nullum erit, nec nautica puppis: Flammat Amen gentes, et Medi Parthique fervent In annis mille, ut ferunt operta Joannis. Nam inde post annos mille gehennae traduntur, Et fabrica cujus erant, cum ipse cremantur.
pass_a_gloss: The trumpet gives a sign to heaven, with the lion removed; And suddenly darknesses happen with a crash of the heaven. The Lord lowers His eyes so that the earth may tremble; He cries out so that all may hear in the world: Behold, I have been silent for a long time, suffering your things. They cry out together, lamenting, groaning late; It is howled, it is wept, and no space is given to the wicked. What will a nursing mother do? since she herself is being burned. The Lord will judge the wicked in the flame of fire: But fire will not touch the just, rather it will cleanse. They linger under one, but part of the sentence has wept. So great will be the heat, that even the stones themselves will melt; The winds come together in lightning, the heavenly anger rages, So that wherever the impious one flees, he is seized by fire. No supply will be, nor a ship's stern: The nations are set aflame, and the Medes and Parthians are fervent In the thousand years, as the secrets of John bear. For from then on, after a thousand years, they are handed over to Gehenna, And the structure of which they were, while they themselves are being burned.
pass_b_english: The trumpet sounds its signal to heaven, the lion lifted up. Suddenly darkness falls with heaven's crash. The Lord lowers his eyes so that the earth trembles. He cries out so that all in the world may hear: Look, I have kept silent a long time, enduring what you have done. Together they scream, weeping, groaning too late. Howling rises, weeping rises, and no room is given to the wicked. What can a nursing mother do, when she herself is burning? The Lord will judge the wicked in the flame of fire, but fire will not touch the righteous — rather it will cleanse them. They linger under one judgment, yet part of the sentence has already wept. The heat will be so great that even stones melt. Winds gather into lightning; heaven's rage roars, so that wherever the impious flees, fire seizes him. No refuge will exist, no ship's stern to save them. The nations blaze; the Medes and Parthians burn in the thousand years, as John's sealed words declare. For after the thousand years they are handed over to Gehenna, and the very structure they belonged to burns while they themselves burn.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the source. The translation of 'sublato leone' as 'the lion removed/lifted up' and 'operta Joannis' as 'secrets/sealed words of John' is faithful. The theological distinction regarding the fire cleansing the just vs judging the wicked is preserved. Scripture allusion to the millennium and John is correctly identified.

source: 'Dat tuba coelo signum, sublato leone; Et fiunt subito tenebrae cum coeli fragore.', english: 'The trumpet gives a sign to heaven, with the lion removed; And suddenly darknesses happen with a crash of the heaven.'
